brief: HSBC reads the Fed's unanimous 25bp September hike, under new Chair Kevin Warsh, as driven by a desire to rebuild inflation-fighting credibility after five-plus years above target and a fresh energy price shock, not by a change in Warsh's no-guidance style. The hawkish dot plot shows 12 of 18 members expecting at least one more 2026 hike, four expecting two, two expecting none, with a large majority seeing 2027 rates settle at 4.00-4.50%. The market prices four total hikes (three more beyond September); HSBC's own view is more dovish, seeing two-to-three total hikes as the sensible ceiling before tightening threatens growth and risk assets, since 100bp of hikes would already leave rates 150bp above neutral. The backdrop is a K-shaped economy: AI investment and wealthy consumers driving growth while other segments lag, plus geopolitical supply shocks. Consequently HSBC expects higher-for-longer rates, treats 10-year UST near 5% as income rather than a hedge, and expects continued dollar weakness to favor non-US equities as US exceptionalism-driven valuations broaden out.
